Subject: Post-call recap — Access controls & support access (RBAC, break-glass, logging)

Hi Samantha / FinTrust security team,

Thanks again for the call today — really appreciate the clarity on your PII boundaries and retention windows. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

- Scope we agreed: Redwood will only receive hashed identifiers + user-provided content for inference. No raw payment card data expected.
- Data residency: primary region requirement is US-East; optional EU region for backups (we noted your controller requirements).
- Retention: default inference logs retained 30 days; you requested options for 7/30/90-day windows and the ability to disable retention for specific routes.
- Access controls: key items to confirm — RBAC model (roles you want), support access policy (break-glass / just-in-time), and audit logs (immutable, retention and export).

Action items: 
1) I will send our RBAC overview and a short playbook for break-glass and support access (Rishi is cc'd to provide the technical detail).
2) Please fill the attached spreadsheet (FinTrust_Security_QA.xlsx) with any additional technical constraints and your preferred retention windows.
3) If helpful, we can schedule a 30-min follow-up next week to align on the support access runbook.

Open questions for you: is customer-managed KMS a hard requirement for this initial POC, or would a Redwood-managed KMS with BYOK planned later be acceptable?

Thanks,

--
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-call recap — Access controls & support access (RBAC, break-glass, logging)

Hi Marissa — thanks for the summary and the spreadsheet. A few clarifications from our side: 

- KMS: For the POC we can accept Redwood-managed KMS if keys are region-restricted to US-East, but for production we need customer-managed KMS (BYOK) and HSM-backed keys.
- RBAC: We want at minimum the following roles scoped to our tenant: Org Admin, Security Admin (audit/export only), App Admin (deploy/config), Read-Only Analyst. Support access must be strictly JIT and require a business justification.
- Break-glass: We will need both a documented break-glass process and proof that every elevated session is logged, with the justification visible and the session linked to an immutable audit entry.
- Audit logs: Log immutability and export (to our S3) are critical. Retention should be configurable per-route.

I've updated the spreadsheet with our preferred retention windows and a few compliance questions — see column D/E. Please confirm whether Redwood supports per-route retention and per-route retention disable.

Also, can you confirm support-account access will be able to be scoped by model and route (so support engineers cannot access customer data outside of scoped troubleshooting)?

Thanks — Samantha

Thanks Samantha — great questions. Quick answers and next steps: 

- KMS: We support Redwood-managed KMS today with region restriction. Customer-managed KMS (BYOK) with HSM is available in Private deployments; it's on the roadmap for Dedicated, and we can include it in the contract for production. I'll flag this on the deal (FT-2026-0421).
- Per-route retention: Yes — Redwood supports per-route retention policies. You can set retention to 0 (disabled) for routes that must not store any inference logs, or 7/30/90 days otherwise.
- Support scoping: Support access can be scoped to tenant + model + route. Default least-privilege is enforced; support roles cannot read data outside the scoped route unless a break-glass escalation is approved.
- Audit logs/export: We provide immutable audit logs, with export to customer S3 and configurable retention. All break-glass actions generate a signed, immutable entry with timestamp, approver, and justification.

I've attached our RBAC playbook and a short diagram (redwood-rbac-playbook.pdf) — Rishi, can you add the technical guardrails for JIT and how the break-glass workflow is implemented (tokening/approval flows, 2FA for approvers, etc.)?

If this looks good, let's schedule the 30-min follow-up for Wed or Thu next week.

Best,

Hi Samantha / team — Rishi here from Security/Applied ML infra. Short technical notes to align expectations and the proposed flow: 

1) RBAC model (tenant-scoped)
   - Roles we expose: org_admin, security_admin (audit/export), app_admin, read_only_analyst, support_jit
   - Each role is scoped to the tenant and can be further scoped to specific models and routes (you get allow-lists on model IDs and route names).

2) Least privilege & service accounts
   - Service accounts for integrations only get tokenized access with limited scope (inference-only, no data export unless explicitly allowed).

3) Support access / Break-glass workflow
   - Default: support engineers have no read access to customer inference payloads.
   - Break-glass: customer can approve a time-limited session via the Console (owner or security_admin must approve). Approval flow requires MFA for approver + a short justification.
   - When break-glass is approved we mint a JIT short-lived credential scoped to the requested model/route and limited time window (e.g., 15/60/240 minutes).
   - All activity in that session is captured and written to an append-only audit log (SHA-256 chain of entries) and a signed artifact is stored and exportable to your S3.

4) Audit & immutability
   - Audit entries are immutable and versioned. We provide a proof bundle (signed entries + sequence) for compliance reviews.
   - Exports to S3 are delivered as gzipped JSONL with checksums; retention policy can be set independently.

5) KMS & keying
   - For Dedicated/Private we support BYOK with HSM integration (Cloud KMS/HSM or on-prem HSM). For hosted customers we offer Redwood-managed keys with region pinning; rotation and export controls are configurable.

6) Implementation notes for your engineers
   - We'll provide a sample policy JSON that maps your requested roles to our role names and an example of how to call the Console API to request a break-glass session.
   - We will also provide logs schema and an example S3 export configuration.

Next steps: Marissa will schedule the 30-min follow-up; I'll prepare the sample policy and the Console API example and drop them in the Drive link (https://drive.redwood.ai/FinTrust/security-onboarding).

Happy to hop on a call if you want to walk through the JIT flow.

Thanks,
--
Rishi Malhotra
